correctness.rationale: Under the cited model, positive effective audience weights smaller than one force xi_i>1. The uniform-prior two-bin equilibrium then has threshold zero and levels +/-1/2. Two prescribed opposite sign branches force x_plus=-(I+D)^(-1)(I-D)Ws/2, uniquely. Since (Ws)_i=s_i(1-2c_i), strict bin membership is exactly c_i>1/2. The two formulas exchange under one F step. On fixed-sign neighborhoods F is affine with derivative D and sup-norm contraction max alpha_i<1, proving full-dimensional local attraction and robust admissible perturbations. The four-node W has positive off-diagonal entries, W^2>0, cross mass 3/4 and for alpha=99/100 amplitude 1/796. A standalone exact Fraction checker passed 1579 finite comparisons. No finite test substitutes for the displayed proof.

originality.rationale: The target 2026 paper explicitly conjectures that sufficiently high inertia forces public-profile stabilization for every initial state, whereas the new theorem derives a strictly attracting complementary-sign two-cycle for all positive inertias below one on a fixed primitive four-node graph. Its necessary-and-sufficient cross-majority criterion is exact, with endogenous uniform-prior two-bin Bayesian posterior levels. Periodic quantized opinions in general are established prior art and not claimed as new. Full-text comparisons with the 2016 state-dependent CODA model and two distinct published opinion-game constructions found no theorem that implies the specific fixed-code all-inertia counterexample.

value.rationale: The originating paper explicitly asks whether high inertia ensures universally settled public discourse. The exact strict-cut criterion answers this negatively for every inertia below one on a fixed primitive network, identifies the structural cause (majority contact to the other public camp), supplies the unique alternating state and an open attraction basin, and explains why numerical tests at high inertia can miss switching as its amplitude shrinks. The result is a motivated, sharp boundary for a published open prediction, not a routine restatement that quantizers can oscillate. It does not claim global dynamical classification or real-world inference.
